'''Pieter Willem''' "'''Piet'''" '''Kasteleyn''' (12 October 1924 – 16 January 1996) was a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[physicist]] famous for his contributions to the field of [[statistical mechanics]].

==Biography==

Pieter Willem Kasteleyn was born in Leiden on 12 October 1924. After finishing high school in 1942, Kasteleyn briefly studied chemistry in Amsterdam. After the war, Leiden University reopened, where he undertook the study of physics and graduated in 1951. He defended his Ph.D. thesis working under S.R. de Groot in 1956.<ref>{{cite web|author=Pieter Kasteleyn |url=http://ilorentz.org/history/proefschriften/sources/Kasteleyn_1956.pdf |title=Statistical problems in ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism and adsorption |year=1956}}</ref>

In 1963 Kasteleyn was nominated Full Professor at the Lorentz Institute of Theoretical Physics in Leiden.
In 1979 he was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.dwc.knaw.nl/biografie/pmknaw/?pagetype=authorDetail&aId=PE00001213 |title=P.W. Kasteleyn (1924 - 1996) |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=24 January 2016}}</ref> From 1981 to 1985 he acted as secretary of the Physics Section of the academy. From 1978 to 1984 he was chairman of the Commission for Theoretical Physics of the Dutch National Physics Foundation. He retired in 1985.

He died on 16 January 1996, after an unexpected and short illness.

==Research==

While investigating dimers on a [[square lattice]] (essentially a [[domino tiling]]), he independently discovered combinatorial [[FKT algorithm|Fisher-Kasteleyn-Temperley algorithm]].<ref>{{citation
 | title = The statistics of dimers on a lattice. I. The number of dimer arrangements on a quadratic lattice
 | journal = Physica
 | volume = 27 | issue = 12 | year = 1961 | pages = 1209–1225
 | first = P. W. | last = Kasteleyn
 | authorlink = Pieter_Kasteleyn
 | doi = 10.1016/0031-8914(61)90063-5}}</ref>
In a series of papers with [[C. M. Fortuin]]<ref>{{cite journal |  title=On the random-cluster model : I. Introduction and relation to other models | doi=10.1016/0031-8914(72)90045-6 | volume=57 |issue = 4| journal=Physica | pages=536–564|year = 1972|last1 = Fortuin|first1 = C.M.|last2 = Kasteleyn|first2 = P.W.}}</ref> he developed [[random cluster model]] and obtained the [[FKG inequality]]. For [[Percolation theory|Bernoulli percolation]] on graphs he formulated the [[Bunkbed conjecture]].
